purpose: Screen public whole-document sources and document source-use boundaries; this is not a dataset, Gold, model run, or readiness result.

baseline.exact_document_id_and_title_scan: No exact match for the screened document IDs/titles was found in the repository at capture time. This is not a semantic overlap proof.

task_fit.current_runtime_unit: One extracted FaultRecord per candidate tree; top event is record.description and tree cause inputs are record.causes.
task_fit.candidate_sources_unit: System-level safety-analysis reports containing multiple top events and complete reference tree diagrams.
task_fit.reason: Passing an entire system report to the current per-record application service would mix multiple systems/events and would not test the same task as a bounded single-record preview.
minimum_evaluation_adapter: Create one bounded, page-addressed input packet per selected top event from eligible upstream prose/FHA/FMECA context; do not include reference tree diagrams, gate symbols, tree-result tables, or derived gate labels in model-visible input.
Retain the full source PDF and SHA-256 outside the model-visible packet; store exact page and quote provenance for every packet segment.
Create a reference graph for the corresponding diagram subgraph, preserving event identity, hierarchy, gates, and source-page locators.

Score two distinct labels: diagram_reference_gate (what the source tree depicts) and text_authorized_gate (AND/OR only when the allowed prose directly supports it; otherwise unknown under the current evidence policy).
Call the result source-held-out evaluation, not a pretraining-isolated or human-expert benchmark; all cases from one report remain one indivisible source cluster.
required_before_final_dataset: Approve event-scope and input-packet rules before creating final labels.
Acquire new whole-document source clusters whose tree pages/labels have not been inspected; the two reviewed reports below are already seen and cannot serve as blind Final.
Freeze the current prompt/model/parser/configuration lock; any later tuning demotes any selected source to development.
Build and validate the evaluation-only adapter without changing production behavior.
Ensure model-visible inputs are disjoint from diagram labels and reference-tree output tables.
Record evidence sufficiency so safe unknown/abstention is not scored as an incorrect AND/OR guess.

independent_final_validation.reason: No blind-eligible source remains from this screen: the two most suitable reports had representative tree pages inspected and are development-only; no bounded source-scope packet, reference graph dataset, or blind model evaluation has been assembled.

review_provenance.primary_review: Repository/source-file inspection, official source metadata, PDF text inspection, and visual inspection of representative tree pages.
review_provenance.independent_contract_review: AI subagent read-only review confirmed the system-report versus per-FaultRecord contract mismatch and the minimum scope-packet adapter requirement.

sources.title: Hazards Analysis and Failure Modes and Effects Criticality Analysis (FMECA) of Four Concept Vehicle Propulsion Systems
sources.source_claim: NASA NTRS describes FHA/FMECA for each of four concept vehicles and says FTA connectivity was developed using FMECA and functional block diagram inputs; the report contains associated tree diagrams.
sources.source_cluster_policy: All four vehicle analyses and diagrams stay within this single report/source cluster; do not split vehicles across Dev and Final. Representative diagram pages have already been inspected, so the entire report is seen-only.
limitations: The diagrams are the reference graph; they do not automatically prove that the allowed prose directly authorizes each AND/OR gate.
Must select bounded top-event scopes and keep FTA diagrams/output labels out of the model-visible packet.
Concept-vehicle domain may require a scope mapping not present in FaultRecord.

sources.title: Single Event Effects Mitigation Techniques Report
sources.source_cluster_policy: The entire FAA report is one source cluster; its tree diagrams and related FTA/result tables must not be split across partitions. Representative diagram pages have already been inspected, so the entire report is seen-only.
traceability_evidence: Section 7.4.2 describes modeling applicable failure conditions in fault trees.
Section 7.5.2 and Tables 52-54 connect failure conditions, basic events, FTA results, and failure-rate justification.
limitations: The report's fault-tree case is a bounded cockpit display system safety analysis inside a broader SEE report.
Exclude Appendix D and answer-revealing FTA synthesis/basic-event tables from model-visible text when testing text-to-tree generation.
Quantitative probability values are out of scope for a qualitative gate-structure benchmark and must not be used as gate labels.

sources.title: Space station safety study - Fault tree analyses
limitations: The volume is primarily fault-tree analyses and does not itself contain all referenced companion system-description inputs.
The inspected scanned diagrams have limited legibility; event-label/OCR confidence needs separate validation.
Not suitable by itself for full original-system-text-to-FTA evaluation.

sources.title: Hubble Space Telescope: SRM/QA observations and lessons learned
sources.reason: Although the NTRS description mentions Appendix D fault-tree analysis, the retrieved 27-page PDF ends in references and contains no Appendix D or tree diagrams. Do not use this retrieved artifact unless the complete matching report is obtained and re-screened.

non_claims: No independent Final dataset or labels have been created.
No current model was called; no model accuracy or calibration result is reported.
No source is allocated to Dev or Final by this screen; the NASA/FAA reports are eligible only for a future development/adapter-validation role, not blind Final.
This screen does not establish semantic non-overlap with existing cases or model pretraining data.
Global fta_ready and production_ready remain false.
